subject: Streaming capacity snapshot & action plan
summary: Post-call recap after initial technical discovery focused on streaming UX and p95 throughput constraints. Confirmed workload profile, p95 targets, concurrency expectations, and next steps for a short POC including required artifacts from the customer and a proposed canary config.
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@spectrahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Taylor <ben.taylor@spectrahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: streaming bottlenecks & p95 targets

Rishi / team — thanks for the call today. Quick write-up from our side so we have alignment.

Pain points:
- End users complain about latency when uploading medical notes and getting structured summaries (esp. during peak hours).
- Our current in-house endpoint shows p95 latency spikes between 700–1,200 ms for 1.5k token requests under load.
- Streaming UX is degraded: first-token for streamed summaries often arrives ~600 ms which hurts perceived responsiveness.

Current stack:
- Inference: single-region Kubernetes with mixed A100 and T4 nodes (autoscaling enabled).
- Frontend multiplexes multiple chats over a single websocket; backend fans out to multiple replicas.
- No prefix caching; we do basic batched requests via a homegrown queueing layer.

Success criteria for a POC:
- Bring p95 for typical 256–768 token summaries down to <=350 ms for non-streamed responses and first-stream-token <=250 ms.
- Support 250 concurrent active users (approx. 120 RPS sustained at 99th percentile) without >3x cost increase.
- Preserve output quality (ROUGE/bleu not acceptable metric alone — we'll use a blind review set).

Artifacts we can share (attached): spectra_request_matrix.xlsx (payload size distribution), network-topology.png. We're preparing anonymized logs — ETA early next week.

Next steps requested from Redwood:
1) A short written plan for a canary/POC: what infra you need, what metrics you'll measure, and a proposed 2-week timeline.
2) Any small config changes we should make to our traffic patterns to make measurements meaningful.
3) Sample cost estimate for the POC run.

Thanks,
Anita
CTO, SpectraHealth

---
Attachments: spectra_request_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-topology.png (image)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Taylor <ben.taylor@spectrahealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 23:18:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: streaming bottlenecks & p95 targets

Anita — really useful notes, thanks for the attachments and for calling this out. Short recap + proposed plan below.

High-level takeaways we heard:
- Goal: reduce p95 for standard summaries to <=350 ms and first-stream-token <=250 ms.
- Workload: mixture of short (<=256 tokens) and medium (256–768 tokens); peak concurrency ~250 active users.
- Constraints: existing autoscaling + mixed GPU fleet, no prefix caching today.

Proposed POC (2 weeks, remote, can start once we have logs):
1) Kickoff + data transfer (2 days): we run a short instrumentation pass against anonymized logs to produce a request-size distribution and latency heatmaps.
2) Canary run (5 days): we deploy a dedicated Redwood canary in your VPC (or our hosted sandbox if you prefer) with:
   - model variant tuned for low-latency (FP16 + optimized kernels),
   - KV-prefix caching enabled for repeated prefixes,
   - batching policy tuned for 99th percentile latency targets (we will cap batch window to avoid P95 regressions),
   - streaming multiplexer to reduce redundant decoding work for overlapping tokens.
3) Analysis & tuning (3 days): compare p50/p95/p99 across request classes, validate streaming first-token latency, and present tuning suggestions.
4) Executive recap + next steps (2 days).

What we need from you:
- Anonymized logs (request size, timestamps, token counts) — you mentioned early next week.
- A small sample of 100 representative prompts (for quality checks).
- Access level decision (VPC peering form vs hosted sandbox).

Quick answers to your asks:
- Canary infra: for 250 concurrent active users we expect to provision 2–4 g4dn/A100-equivalent devices depending on exact sequence length distribution; we'll provide a tighter estimate post-log analysis.
- Cost estimate: preliminary rough ballpark of $X–$Y for the 2-week POC (we'll follow up with a detailed break-down).

I've looped in Monica (SE) to propose the exact benchmark harness and the instrumentation details. We'll follow up with a suggested kickoff slot once we get the logs.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Ben Taylor <ben.taylor@spectrahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 01:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: streaming bottlenecks & p95 targets (technical notes)

Anita — quick technical clarifications and what we'll benchmark.

What we'll measure (per-request class):
- First-byte (TTFB) for streaming start, streaming-first-token latency, end-to-end completion latency (p50/p95/p99).
- GPU utilization, batch sizes, batch wait times, and KV cache hit rate.
- Network RTT distribution (client -> ingress -> pod) and serialization overhead.

Suggested config for canary (initial):
- Model: open-variant-4b-fp16 (or your preferred transformer) with tuned kernels.
- Batching: max batch size = 32, dynamic batching with 10 ms window on short requests; 25 ms for medium. We'll cap batch wait to avoid p95 blowups.
- Concurrency handle: target per-replica concurrency 16–24 for A100-class, 6–8 for T4-class; we'll bias assignment to higher-performance GPUs.
- Streaming: enable prefix KV cache + multiplexing for overlapping sessions; ensure we stream flushed tokens every 50ms to maintain UX.

Data we need from you:
- Anonymized trace sample (we can accept a gzipped tar of logs): spectra_anonymized_logs.tar.gz.
- Authentication key for the sandbox endpoint (if you choose hosted).

I'll prepare a small benchmark harness we can run in your environment and a matching dashboard (token-level latency breakdown). Est. time to prepare harness: 48 hours after we receive logs.

Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai

---
Attachment stub: benchmark_plan.md (will send separately)

From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@spectrahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Taylor <ben.taylor@spectrahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: streaming bottlenecks & p95 targets

Thanks Rishi + Monica — this is exactly what we needed. Quick confirmations:
- We'll deliver the anonymized logs by Monday 2027-04-12 (link to Drive in related links).
- Spectra can run the benchmark harness in our staging VPC; we'll submit the VPC peering request today and share the form.
- Priority: first-token streaming latency is the highest business impact measure; p95 <=250 ms would be a stretch goal but our baseline target is <=350 ms.

Ben and I discussed internal reviewer availability; we can allocate two SMEs for the benchmark windows.

Please send the proposed kickoff time slots and a draft SOW / POC cost estimate that we can review with procurement.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to results.

-Anita
CTO, SpectraHealth
